Placemaker.Beach.Name: Beach
Placemaker.Recipe.Beach.Description: Real sand painted into the terrain from the water's edge, blending into the grass behind; umbrellas in loose rows, lifeguard posts, a promenade with short accesses onto landings, dunes behind.
Placemaker.Beach.style.Tooltip: Sandy, rocky (dirt texture with sand pockets), river, cove (wild dunes) or volleyball beach. Each lays out the shore differently.
Placemaker.Beach.waterSide.Tooltip: Which side of the area faces the water. Automatic finds the water; otherwise pick a side (north = +Z on the map).
Placemaker.Beach.beachDepth.Tooltip: How far the sand reaches inland from the waterline to the back path.
Placemaker.Beach.umbrellas.Tooltip: Umbrella sets (an umbrella with loungers) per hectare of sand.
Placemaker.Beach.layout.Tooltip: Loose groups like a public beach, or tidy rows like a resort lido.
Placemaker.Beach.carve.Tooltip: Grade the ground into one smooth gentle slope down to the waterline and on under the water (permanent): it lowers the ground and only fills small hollows; cliffs are left natural.
Placemaker.Beach.slope.Tooltip: Gradient of the carved beach. Real sand beaches are 2–8 %.
Placemaker.Beach.wetBand.Tooltip: Strip along the water kept free of umbrellas (boats, rocks and tide pools go here).
Placemaker.Beach.sandSurface.Tooltip: Also lay a sand surface over the beach (hard edged). Off by default: the sand is painted into the terrain instead. Useful on custom maps whose terrain layer 4 is not sand.
Placemaker.Beach.sandBlend.Tooltip: How far the sand texture fades into the ground behind the beach. Small = a crisp edge at the promenade, large = sand drifting far inland.
Placemaker.Beach.sandReach.Tooltip: Carry the sand and the graded slope past the outline down to the real water and on under it (see Sand under water), so the beach meets the water even when the area was drawn short of it (permanent).
Placemaker.Beach.paint.Tooltip: Paint the beach into the terrain texture like the game's Paint texture tool, with a soft blend (permanent).
Placemaker.Beach.paintLayer.Tooltip: Which terrain texture to paint: 1 dry grass, 2 lush grass, 3 dirt, 4 sand (on vanilla maps; custom maps may differ).
Placemaker.Beach.backdrop.Tooltip: What lies behind the back path: dunes with marram grass, a lawn, woods, or nothing.
Placemaker.Beach.duneDepth.Tooltip: How deep the dune belt (or the planted strip) is behind the back path.
Placemaker.Beach.duneFence.Tooltip: Short fence runs along the dune foot where the ground is even, with gaps where paths cross. Off by default: vanilla has no timber sand fence.
Placemaker.Beach.grassDensity.Tooltip: How much grass and scrub grows on the dunes or along the backdrop edge.
Placemaker.Beach.backPath.Tooltip: A path behind the sand, parallel to the water, with benches, lamps, huts and kiosks.
Placemaker.Beach.accessSpacing.Tooltip: Distance between the short accesses from the promenade down onto the sand.
Placemaker.Beach.benchSpacing.Tooltip: Benches facing the sea along the back path. 0 = none.
Placemaker.Beach.landings.Tooltip: A small deck or paved landing at the end of each beach access, where the path meets the sand.
Placemaker.Beach.huts.Tooltip: Small groups of changing huts, or a long row of beach huts behind the back path.
Placemaker.Beach.lifeguards.Tooltip: Lifeguard posts behind the wet sand, facing the water (a tall chair, lifebuoy and flag unless you pick a lifeguard tower asset).
Placemaker.Beach.courts.Tooltip: Volleyball courts on the sand, parallel to the water. The volleyball beach adds some automatically.
Placemaker.Beach.jetties.Tooltip: Timber jetties from the sand out over the water, in line with an access path. They may reach past the outline over the water.
Placemaker.Beach.jettyLength.Tooltip: How far each jetty reaches out from the sand (it stops where the water ends).
Placemaker.Beach.jettyHead.Tooltip: A cross deck at the end of each jetty to swim from.
Placemaker.Beach.bay.Tooltip: Carves a bay into the land below the water level, so the water flows in and the shore curves. 0 keeps the shore as drawn.
Placemaker.Beach.boats.Tooltip: Rowing boats and kayaks pulled up on the wet sand.
Placemaker.Beach.fires.Tooltip: Fire pits with seats around them on the sand.
Placemaker.Beach.rockClusters.Tooltip: Groups of rocks; on a rocky beach they straddle the waterline, in a cove they also form headlands.
Placemaker.Beach.tidePools.Tooltip: Shallow hollows near the waterline ringed by rocks (permanent terrain change).
Placemaker.Beach.Issue.NoCourtSpace: The beach is too shallow for volleyball courts.
Placemaker.Beach.Issue.FewerCourts: Only {0} of {1} volleyball courts fit on the sand.
Placemaker.Shore.Issue.NoWater: No water found next to the area: it faces away from the road (or the longest edge). Set Water side to choose.
Placemaker.Shore.Issue.WaterInside: Much of the area is water: only the dry part is built on.
Placemaker.AddOn.BeachBar.Name: Beach bar
Placemaker.AddOn.BeachBar.tables.Tooltip: Cafe tables on the terrace in front of each bar.
Placemaker.Shore.Issue.Cliff: {0}% of this shore is cliff: the cliff face is left natural, with a cliff-top walk and lookouts there instead.
Placemaker.Shore.Issue.Earthwork: The ground was only reshaped within limits (cut up to {0} m, fill up to {1} m): the design follows the terrain where it would have needed more.
Placemaker.Beach.underwater.Tooltip: How far the sand and the gentle beach slope continue under the water past the waterline (permanent).
Placemaker.Beach.berm.Tooltip: The low crest the waves build at the top of the wet sand, with a soft hollow behind it (permanent terrain change).
Placemaker.Beach.storms.Tooltip: Ridges thrown up by storms, stepping up the beach one behind the other, with scalloped cusps along the water. Shingle beaches have two or three.
Placemaker.Beach.headlands.Tooltip: Rock headlands built out into the water at both ends of the shore, piled with boulders, a cove between them. How far they reach out (0 = none).
Placemaker.Beach.platforms.Tooltip: Share of the shore with flat rock shelves just above the water, with tide pools and weed.
Placemaker.Beach.bluff.Tooltip: Raises the land behind the beach into a high bank this tall (permanent terrain change).
Placemaker.Beach.ravines.Tooltip: Deep gullies (barrancas) cut through the bank down to the water, choked with boulders. The walk crosses them on footbridges.
Placemaker.Beach.knolls.Tooltip: Rounded rock domes on the beach and out in the shallows, crowned with boulders.
Placemaker.Beach.boulders.Tooltip: Loose boulders per hectare, in clumps over the beach and out in the shallow water.
Placemaker.Beach.channels.Tooltip: Creeks winding in from the water through a marsh flat, with salt pans and reed beds along them (permanent terrain change).
Placemaker.Beach.blowouts.Tooltip: Gaps the wind has cut through the dunes, their sand thrown in a mound behind each.
Placemaker.Beach.hummocks.Tooltip: Breaks the back dunes into knobs and hollows instead of a smooth roll.
Placemaker.Beach.boardwalk.Tooltip: A timber boardwalk from the promenade out over the sand or the marsh to the water, ending in a T.
Placemaker.Beach.Issue.NoWater: No water touches this area, so nothing reaches a shore. Best: draw the area from the land down into a lake, a river or the sea, overlapping the water by 10–20 m.
Placemaker.Beach.Issue.ShortShore: Only {0} m of shore: a beach needs 40 m or more along the water to look like one. Draw the area longer along the waterline.
Placemaker.Beach.Issue.NarrowLand: Only {0} m of land behind the water: no room for the sand, a walk and what stands behind it. Draw the area 30–60 m inland.
Placemaker.Beach.Issue.SteepShore: The bank down to the water is steep ({0} %): the beach is carved into it and its back stays a high bank. A gentler stretch looks more natural, or pick Rocky ravine or Granite shore.
Placemaker.Beach.Issue.CliffAdvice: On a cliff a small pocket beach is cut into the rock, with a path down a gully. For a long beach, move the area to a lower stretch of the shore.
Placemaker.Beach.Issue.IslandsOutside: No island fits: draw the area about 50 m out over the water to get one.
Placemaker.Beach.islands.Tooltip: Low rocky islets off the beach, each reached by a timber footbridge with a bench at the top (permanent terrain change).
